observations.explanation: The paper defines four modules—profile, memory, planning, and action—and says that disabling modules lets the majority of prior studies be viewed within the framework (PDF pp. 2–3). This supports the claim that it is a compact organizing structure connected to much prior work.

Evaluation is treated in a dedicated section, distinguishing subjective and objective evaluation and discussing multiple methods, metrics, strategies, and benchmarks (PDF pp. 19–21). The cited statement also explicitly presents objective evaluation as complementary to human assessment (PDF p. 21).
The authors explicitly call the field “still at its initial stage” and state that many challenges remain, then discuss those challenges in detail (PDF pp. 22–23).

The paper says current techniques have limitations in measuring general capabilities and calls for continued progress in evaluation methodology (PDF p. 21), supporting the general concern. But it does not specifically establish that measures across domains need to be reconciled or validated; that part is a plausible open question rather than a demonstrated unresolved defect.
